How it was built

A LangGraph research agent, run per app through Composio MCP, writing schema-constrained findings to an append-only SQLite store — not a hand-filled spreadsheet.

apps_seed.csv (100 apps, fixed)
→
orchestrator.py (concurrency 5)
→
research_agent per app (LangGraph)
→
SQLite, append-only per pass
→
build_report.py
→
this static page + embedded JSON

Research agent (LangGraph)

Each app is one state-graph run: SearchDocs → FetchPage → ExtractFields → ScoreConfidence → ValidateSchema → Persist, with a bounded retry loop back to SearchDocs on low confidence (max 2 retries) and a FlagForHuman exit for anything that still won't resolve. Extraction is schema-constrained JSON against the AppFinding Pydantic model, never free text — a field the model can't ground in a fetched page comes back null plus a blocker string rather than a guess.

Tool access — Composio MCP

Search and fetch tools are called through Composio-hosted MCP servers as the primary path. If a tool call is flaky, the agent falls back to a direct httpx/playwright call, logged as mcp_fallback=true on that finding, so the report can disclose how much of the run actually went through MCP versus a fallback.

Confidence scoring

Each finding carries a confidence score: a weighted blend of whether the evidence URL sits on the app's own docs domain, the model's self-reported certainty per field, and whether more than one page agreed. confidence < 0.7 triggers a retry with a refined query before the row is persisted.

Append-only persistence

Every finding is a new row keyed by (app_id, run_id, pass_number) — never an in-place update. That's what lets a later verification pass show an honest "before" state instead of silently overwriting pass 1.

Verification design

A stratified sample — 2 apps per category, 20 total — is independently re-researched by verifier_agent.py using browser-use from a blank context, with no visibility into pass-1 output, producing a field-by-field match/mismatch table. Mismatches trigger a pass-2 re-research; a 10-app manual spot-check against live docs is the human check on the cross-checker.

Outbound MCP server

agents/mcp_server.py re-exposes the finished dataset itself as MCP tools — get_app_record, list_findings, get_pattern_summary, get_verification_report — so the same "apps become agent-callable tools" idea this dataset is about also applies to the pipeline's own output.

LayerChoiceWhy
OrchestrationLangGraphReal branches (retry / flag-human) are clearer as an explicit graph than nested conditionals, and it gives per-node execution traces for debugging.
StorageSQLite, append-onlyZero provisioning inside a 6–8h budget; append-only preserves the pre-verification "before" state for an honest accuracy story.
Verification toolbrowser-use (sample only)A different tool cross-checking the fast pass is a real independent check, not the same method run twice; reserved for the sample to stay inside the time budget.
ReportStatic dist/index.htmlNo server to keep alive, no cold start; opens standalone even offline, with the full dataset embedded as JSON for machine consumption.
Verification (the stratified 20-app cross-check and 10-app human spot-check) is built into the pipeline but has not been run against this dataset yet — see scripts/run_verification.py. Findings above are pass-1 only.
